security_audit.summary: All 39 static detections are false positives caused by Markdown formatting, relative documentation links, metadata URLs, and marketing terminology. The skill processes user-provided analytics exports, treats them as untrusted evidence, and requests consent before saving a report. No prompt injection, command execution, path traversal, or data-exfiltration intent was found.

remediation.issue: Static scanners interpret Markdown backticks and relative links as command execution or path traversal.
remediation.suggestion: Keep documentation links and code examples clearly separated from executable instructions; avoid shell-like examples when a plain-language prompt is sufficient.

remediation.issue: The skill can save reports to memory after consent.
remediation.suggestion: Continue requiring explicit user approval before saving and constrain generated filenames to a fixed skill-owned directory.

content.value_statement: Paid campaigns can waste budget when events, UTMs, and attribution settings are incomplete. This skill produces an evidence-based pre-flight checklist and a reusable UTM and event specification.
actual_capabilities: Reviews user-provided GA4 conversions and traffic-acquisition exports.
Creates a pass, fail, or needs-input tracking pre-flight checklist.
Checks a manual test conversion for event name, value, and source attribution.
Builds a UTM naming convention and conversion-event specification.
Flags cross-platform deduplication and attribution-window gaps.
Identifies offline conversion and iOS-ATT modeled-data limitations.
limitations: It does not access ad platforms, pixels, tag managers, or analytics accounts directly.
It relies on exports and test results supplied by the user.
It does not calculate reconciled double counting or incrementality.
It does not score ROAS readiness or make budget decisions.

use_cases.title: Prepare a campaign launch
use_cases.description: Check whether conversion measurement is ready before a paid campaign begins.

use_cases.title: Standardize tracking across channels
use_cases.description: Create consistent UTM and event rules for Google, Meta, and analytics reporting.

use_cases.title: Investigate reporting differences
use_cases.description: Identify likely UTM, event, deduplication, or attribution-window gaps before escalation.

prompt_templates.title: Check a launch setup
prompt_templates.prompt: Create a pre-launch conversion tracking checklist for my Google Ads campaign. My main conversion is a purchase.

prompt_templates.title: Create tracking standards
prompt_templates.prompt: Build a UTM naming convention and conversion-event specification for a Meta and Google lead-generation campaign.

prompt_templates.title: Review supplied exports
prompt_templates.prompt: Review my GA4 Conversions and Traffic-acquisition exports. Mark each tracking pre-flight item as pass, fail, or needs-input.

prompt_templates.title: Assess cross-platform signals
prompt_templates.prompt: For Google and Meta, identify deduplication gates and attribution-window alignment issues from these exports. Do not calculate a reconciliation.

output_examples.input: Check tracking for a Google and Meta purchase campaign.
output: Fail: no completed manual test conversion is recorded.
Needs input: attribution windows were not provided.
UTM standard: use lowercase source, medium, and campaign values.

output_examples.input: Build a UTM and event specification for a lead campaign.
output: UTM rule: use paid_social for Meta traffic and cpc for search traffic.
Event rule: use one canonical generate_lead event with a stable lead identifier.
Flag: do not include names, email addresses, or order details in UTMs.

best_practices: Provide recent GA4 conversion and traffic-acquisition exports.
Complete one real manual test conversion before the review.
Use the resulting event and UTM specification across every paid channel.
anti_patterns: Do not mark items as passed without exported evidence or a test conversion.
Do not place personal data or order details in UTM parameters.
Do not compare platform totals without documenting attribution windows and a source of truth.

faq.question: Does this skill connect to my analytics account?
faq.answer: No. It reviews exports and information that you provide.

faq.question: Which platforms can it support?
faq.answer: It can prepare checks for Google, Meta, and other platforms with conversion exports.

faq.question: What data should I provide?
faq.answer: Provide GA4 conversions, traffic-acquisition exports, platform names, and a manual test conversion result.

faq.question: Can it fix my pixel automatically?
faq.answer: No. It identifies evidence gaps and lists the configuration work to complete.

faq.question: Does it reconcile Meta and Google conversions?
faq.answer: No. It checks that a deduplication rule and routing process exist before launch.

faq.question: Does it recommend increasing ad spend?
faq.answer: No. It verifies measurement readiness and does not score ROAS or budget decisions.
